children: Distance limits the Canadian Prime Minister's push for "associate membership" of the European bloc. Yet interests are aligned for closer links. Ottawa wants to diversify beyond the US, which takes 72% of its exports. Brussels needs energy, critical minerals and security partners.

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney wants to deepen the country's ties with the European Union, the Wall Street Journal reported on September 12 citing people familiar with the matter. Though this relationship would fall short of full membership of the bloc or its common market, it could grant the North American country the title of "Associate Member of the European Union.”

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen could announce the new strategic pact during her State of the Union address in Strasbourg on September 16. Carney is scheduled to address the European Parliament on September 17.
